entities.summary: Pedro Téllez-Girón, 1st Duke of Osuna, 5th count of Ureña, was a Spanish nobleman and administrator who played a crucial role in the development of the Spanish Empire during the early modern period. Born into the aristocracy, he rose to prominence through his service to the Spanish crown and his strategic marriages, ultimately becoming a key figure in the administration of the Spanish territories in Europe and the Americas. Téllez-Girón's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped shape the trajectory of Spanish colonization and the growth of the Habsburg Empire. His influence can be seen in the establishment of the Spanish Inquisition, the colonization of the Americas, and the spread of Christianity throughout the New World. As a member of the Spanish nobility, Téllez-Girón embodied the values of honor, loyalty, and duty that defined the aristocracy of early modern Europe. He died on September 13, 1590, at the age of 64, leaving behind a legacy that continues to be felt to this day. The Osuna duchy, which he inherited, became a major power in southern Spain, and his descendants continued to play a significant role in Spanish politics and society for centuries to come. Téllez-Girón's life and legacy serve as a testament to the enduring power of the Spanish Empire and the complexities of the early modern European experience.

entities.summary:
Pedro Téllez-Girón, 1st Duke of Osuna, 5th count of Ureña, was a Spanish nobleman and administrator born on August 8, 1537, in Osuna, Spain, and died on September 13, 1590.

As a key figure in the Spanish nobility, Pedro Téllez-Girón played a crucial role in the governance of the Habsburg Empire during the late 16th century.

His tenure as Duke of Osuna was marked by significant events, including the defeat of the Moorish army at the Battle of Lepanto in 1571, which secured Spanish dominance over the Mediterranean.

Pedro Téllez-Girón's legacy extends to the modern era, with his descendant, the 8th Duke of Osuna, continuing to hold the title to this day.

This Duke's life was immortalized in the 19th-century novel 'Osuna: The Duke' by José María de Azcárraga.

The Osuna family's wealth and influence were so great that they were able to commission the construction of the impressive Osuna Palace, a testament to their status as one of Spain's most prominent noble families.

Pedro Téllez-Girón's contributions to the Spanish Empire have been recognized as a key factor in its expansion during the 16th century, earning him a place among the most influential figures of the time.

The Duke's efforts to promote trade and commerce between Spain and its colonies also contributed to the growth of the Spanish economy.

Despite his significant contributions, Pedro Téllez-Girón's life was cut short, leaving behind a legacy that continues to shape the history of Spain and its people.

Pedro Téllez-Girón's story is a testament to the enduring power of family, duty, and service, inspiring generations of nobles and commoners alike.
